before.heading: A compact traveling kitchen
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Crop and fruit-tree captures are included. Still needed: a traveling kitchen with reusable tools and ingredients, plus a JEI example of a recommended meal and its intermediate steps.

after.heading: A compact traveling kitchen
after.body: Keep reusable tools near a supply of repeatable ingredients. Look up a final meal in JEI, then follow each crafted ingredient back to its recipe. The Cook Book lists thermal effects beside the affected meals, so your kitchen can support both hunger and climate.

before.heading: BlueMap: read the threat
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Capture KNCraft BlueMap showing both Wither Storm markers, a named settlement or landmark, and enough terrain to judge direction. Hide private chat or unrelated browser tabs. This should teach players how to plan a route

before.heading: BlueMap: read the threat
before.body: around the current threats.

after.heading: BlueMap: read the threat
after.body: Three Wither Storm markers appear near the center of this BlueMap example. Check the live map before traveling; positions change.

after.heading: The three markers
after.body: Three markers in the same map. Check live positions before choosing a route.

before.heading: One camp, two locations
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Capture a furnished tent interior, the packed item with Tent ID visible, and the same interior after setting up elsewhere. Include a simple arrangement of storage, cooking, temperature supplies and a clear door. This

before.heading: One camp, two locations
before.body: demonstrates what persists during a move.

after.heading: One camp, two locations
after.body: A tent keeps its interior when packed and pitched again. Check the packed item's Tent ID so you move the same camp. Keep the door clear and inspect the new campsite climate after moving; furniture persistence does not guarantee a comfortable temperature.

before.heading: Weather to recognize
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Storm, tornado, snow and siren captures are included. Still needed: a Deflector setup showing its placement. No extra HUD capture is needed.

after.heading: Weather to recognize
after.body: Place a Deflector as part of your shelter plan, and use the Weather2 instruments described in this chapter to watch changing conditions. A device does not replace a planned route back to shelter.

before.heading: Symbiont opening
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Capture a Withered Symbiont in its weakened posture from behind, with the purple weak point clearly visible. Add a second capture of the same encounter with the boss bar showing KNCraft health scaling. Keep

before.heading: Symbiont opening
before.body: this separate from the Aether and Depths spoiler-free sections.

after.heading: Symbiont opening
after.body: Watch for the weakened posture, then look behind the Symbiont for its exposed purple weak point. Coordinate your attack window with nearby players. A boss bar shows remaining health; it does not by itself establish maximum-health scaling.

before.heading: Find the entrance
before.body: SCREENSHOT NEEDED. Capture the open entrance above the main head at a readable distance, with the full opening visible. A second image should show a safe aiming position. This is a navigation image; avoid motion blur and hide chat.

after.heading: Find the entrance
after.body: Look for the open entrance above the main head. Identify the whole opening before committing to an approach. Keep your group informed of its position; reaching the entrance does not make the approach safe from attacks.

before.heading: One camp, two locations
before.body: A tent keeps its interior when packed and pitched again. Check the packed item's Tent ID so you move the same camp. Keep the door clear and inspect the new campsite climate after moving; furniture persistence does not guarantee a comfortable temperature.

after.heading: One camp, two locations
after.body: Pack through the tent door with a Tent Mallet, then pitch it at the next campsite. Check the packed item's Tent ID to keep the same interior. Your furniture stays with the tent, but its ambient climate follows the new outdoor entrance.

after.heading: First campsite
after.body: The first tent stands in open grassland. Its doorway leads to the furnished interior shown next.

after.heading: Inside the first camp
after.body: Storage, workstations and a central hearth make a portable camp. Leave a clear path to the door.

after.heading: A colder campsite
after.body: At the snowy second campsite, frost covers the screen. Moving a tent also changes its source climate.

after.heading: Inside, hearth off
after.body: The furnishings remain, but the cold persists inside. The tent shell alone does not provide a moderate climate.

after.heading: Inside, hearth on
after.body: The active hearth warms this camp. Fuel, warm-up time and a clear path for its effect still matter.

after.heading: Cold camp: hearth off
after.body: The environment readout at the right shows 22 in this capture; the blue body display and frost show cold stress. These are different readings. Your temperatures depend on the campsite and conditions.

after.heading: Cold camp: hearth on
after.body: After the hearth runs, the environment readout shows 61 and the central body display returns to 0 in this example. Give the hearth time to work. These readings are examples, not a guaranteed target temperature.

before.heading: Symbiont opening
before.body: Watch for the weakened posture, then look behind the Symbiont for its exposed purple weak point. Coordinate your attack window with nearby players. A boss bar shows remaining health; it does not by itself establish maximum-health scaling.

after.heading: Find the weak point
after.body: Wait for the Symbiont to slump into its weakened posture. Move around behind it and aim at the exposed purple area on its back. Strike during this opening. When it recovers, return to dodging its spells and dealing with summoned enemies.

before.heading: Find the entrance
before.body: Look for the open entrance above the main head. Identify the whole opening before committing to an approach. Keep your group informed of its position; reaching the entrance does not make the approach safe from attacks.

after.heading: Find the Bowels entrance
after.body: Face the largest, central head and look above it for an open hole in the storm body. Wait until the opening is visible. Aim an Ender Pearl into the hole; a crossbow can launch it farther. Bring your Command Block tool and fall protection.
